package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affects the version running on Smith & Wesson's website at the time of attack)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected code is designed to steal customer payment data by skimming sensitive information from the checkout process and exfiltrating it to an attacker-controlled server. This is a classic example of a web skimmer/Magecart-style attack, which is always considered malicious as it directly targets user financial data and compromises the integrity of the e-commerce platform.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user submits the checkout or payment form
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the Magento website frontend JavaScript, likely within a checkout or payment template file (e.g., checkout.phtml or payment.phtml)
required_permissions: Access to the DOM to read form fields
Ability to initiate outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from the browser

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user submits the checkout form, the code hooks into the form submission event, reads credit card number, expiration date, and CVV from the DOM, and sends this data via an HTTP POST request to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts sensitive payment data directly from the checkout form and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled server, which is a definitive indicator of a web skimming attack. Such behavior is never legitimate in a production e-commerce environment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout JavaScript should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors or gateways, never to unknown or untrusted third-party domains. Any code that exfiltrates sensitive data outside the merchant's or payment processor's infrastructure violates PCI DSS and e-commerce security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may collect payment data to send to authorized payment gateways or for fraud detection, but only to documented, trusted endpoints and never to domains not associated with the merchant or payment processor.
key_indicators: Hooks into form submission events specifically on checkout or payment pages
Reads sensitive payment fields such as credit card number, expiration date, and CVV from the DOM
Sends collected payment data to an external, non-standard domain not associated with the merchant
Presence of injected or obfuscated JavaScript code not found in the official Magento codebase
Outbound network requests from the browser to domains unrelated to payment processing

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Magento platform to gain unauthorized write access to website files.
Malicious JavaScript skimmer code is injected into the checkout or payment page template files (e.g., checkout.phtml or payment.phtml).
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in user browsers

attack_chain.action: When a customer submits payment information, the skimmer code intercepts the data from the form and sends it to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of payment data to attacker-controlled infrastructure

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into checkout or payment form submission events
Client-side code accessing DOM elements containing payment or personal information (e.g., credit card fields)
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from browser JavaScript to untrusted or unknown domains, especially during checkout
file_indicators: Unexpected changes or additions in Magento template files such as checkout.phtml or payment.phtml
Presence of obfuscated or minified JavaScript code not matching the official Magento codebase
Injected <script> tags or inline event handlers in checkout-related pages that are not part of the standard deployment
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the merchant or payment processor (e.g., attacker-domain.com/collect)
Unusual traffic patterns from checkout or payment pages to external IPs or domains, especially those not previously seen in legitimate operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for unauthorized modifications to Magento template files, particularly those related to checkout or payment. Use web application firewalls or browser instrumentation to detect JavaScript accessing payment fields and sending data to unknown domains. Analyze network traffic from checkout pages for suspicious outbound requests to non-whitelisted domains. Regularly compare deployed JavaScript files against known-good baselines to identify unauthorized changes or injected code.
